mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate (measured as the 3-month trailing change in FEDFUNDS) is associated with positive S&P 500 forward 20-day returns, as lower rates reduce the discount rate for equity valuation and stimulate economic activity.
failure_condition: In periods where FEDFUNDS declines by at least 0.25 percentage points over the prior 3 months, the S&P 500 produces negative 20-day forward returns in more than 50% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 5.0% in the most recent month signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which typically precede corporate earnings slowdowns and lead to negative S&P 500 forward 20-day returns.
failure_condition: When UNRATE exceeds 5.0%, the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day forward returns in more than 50% of such instances.

mechanism_narrative: High inflation (CPIAUCSL > 3.0% year-over-year) combined with a stable or declining federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS change <= 0.0%) signals inadequate monetary policy response to inflation, increasing stagflation risk and leading to negative S&P 500 forward 20-day returns.
failure_condition: In periods where CPIAUCSL exceeds 3.0% and FEDFUNDS change is <= 0.0%, the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day forward returns in more than 50% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: In high-inflation regimes (CPIAUCSL > 3.0%), a decline in industrial production (INDPRO < 95.0) signals worsening supply conditions that lead to negative S&P 500 forward 20-day returns due to stagflation concerns.
failure_condition: In periods where CPIAUCSL > 3.0% and INDPRO < 95.0, the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day forward returns in more than 50% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in housing starts (HOUST) over the past 3 months signals strong consumer demand and economic expansion, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward 20-day returns as corporate earnings benefit from a robust economy.
failure_condition: In periods where HOUST has increased by at least 1.0% over the prior 3 months, the S&P 500 produces negative 20-day forward returns in more than 50% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in monthly non-farm payrolls (PAYEMS) below 50,000 new jobs signals a weakening labor market, which typically precedes reduced consumer spending and negative S&P 500 forward 20-day returns.
failure_condition: When PAYEMS growth is below 50,000, the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day forward returns in more than 50% of such instances.

mechanism_narrative: Strong real personal consumption (RSAFS > 1.5% year-over-year) combined with a declining federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS change < 0.0%) signals robust economic growth supported by accommodative monetary policy, leading to positive S&P 500 forward 20-day returns.
failure_condition: In periods where RSAFS exceeds 1.5% and FEDFUNDS declines, the S&P 500 produces negative 20-day forward returns in more than 50% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: In the early recovery phase of an economic cycle (as indicated by the first positive GDP growth after a recession), a rebound in quarterly GDP growth (GDPC1) above 0.5% leads to positive S&P 500 forward 60-day returns as the market prices in the recovery.
failure_condition: In the early recovery phase (defined as the first quarter of positive GDP growth after a recession), when GDPC1 growth exceeds 0.5%, the S&P 500 produces negative 60-day forward returns in more than 50% of cases.
